title: Watch: Ceddanne Rafaela hits home runs in back-to-back at-bats
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Ceddanne Rafaela hit two home runs in his first two at-bats against the Dodgers on Saturday.
Rafaela's homers tied the game after Dodgers' Teoscar Hernandez hit a go-ahead two-run homer.
Rafaela now has 14 home runs this season, including a crucial homer the night before against the Dodgers.

title: Red Sox reportedly attempted to acquire shortstop Elly De La Cruz, turned down by Reds
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: The Boston Red Sox made a substantial offer to acquire Cincinnati Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz.
The proposed trade package from the Red Sox mainly included prospects but was ultimately rejected by the Reds.
Despite injuries, Boston continues exploring options to strengthen their middle infield before the trade deadline.

title: Drake Maye says his shoulder ‘feels great’ as Patriots training camp continues
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Drake Maye confirms his throwing shoulder feels great as New England Patriots' training camp progresses.
Patriots added wide receiver A.J. Brown to bolster offensive options for the new season.
Maye and Brown developing on-field chemistry ahead of Patriots' 2026-27 season opener against Seahawks.

title: If July’s stretch of dominance wasn’t enough, the Red Sox’ win Friday proved they’re plenty capable of a postseason run
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: The Boston Red Sox defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 5-4 on Friday night despite missing key player Willson Contreras.
Ceddanne Rafaela's performance turned a 4-3 deficit into a 5-4 victory, supported by strong plays from Jarren Duran and Andruw Monasterio.
With recent success and trade deadline approaching, the Red Sox are positioned as strong contenders for a postseason run.

title: Red Sox fend off Dodgers, 9-4, in grindy series opener
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Ceddanne Rafaela hit a go-ahead two-run homer, leading the Red Sox to a 9-4 victory over the Dodgers.
Brayan Bello pitched four scoreless innings in relief, improving his MLB-leading relief ERA to 0.69.
The Red Sox secured their 21st win of July, marking their best monthly win record in franchise history.

title: Gabe Jacas makes his Patriots debut and other takeaways from Day 7 of training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Gabe Jacas, Patriots' 2026 second-round pick, made his practice debut on Saturday in a limited role.
Patriots' defense recorded two interceptions during Day 7 of training camp, balancing Drake Maye's offensive success.
Undrafted rookie Tanner Arkin is emerging as a potential backup tight end, earning first-team reps due to his blocking skills.

title: Mass. to be 4th state to roll out EBT chip cards to curb fraud
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Massachusetts to issue chip-enabled EBT cards statewide to prevent SNAP benefit theft, becoming the fourth state to do so.
Nearly 1 million Massachusetts residents use EBT cards at 5,500 authorized retailers, with $2.6 billion distributed annually.
Recipients must activate new EBT cards within 60 days; retailers are updating systems to accept chip-and-tap transactions.

title: Boston is now offering ‘pet certificates’ for couples who wed at City Hall
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Boston City Hall now offers 'pet certificates' for couples marrying with pets present at the ceremony.
Mayor Michelle Wu introduced the 'pet certificate' program to recognize pets as part of couples' households.
The certificate is titled 'Family Companion Status Record' and celebrates pets with the 'Paw of Approval.'

title: Kevin Nealon discusses Conan, Dunkin’, SNL and more ahead of local shows
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Kevin Nealon is performing in Boston and Portsmouth, New Hampshire, highlighting his comedy style and local connections.
Nealon has embraced social media for comedy, promoting his stand-up special 'Loose in the Crotch' on YouTube.
Known for his SNL roles, Nealon continues to collaborate with Adam Sandler and explores new ventures like 'Hiking with Kevin.'

title: Red Sox’ Willson Contreras leaves game after scary HBP vs. Dodgers
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras was hit in the helmet by a 95 MPH pitch from Dodgers' Will Klein.
Contreras stayed in the game briefly but was replaced defensively in the next inning for precautionary reasons.
Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy reported that Contreras is doing well but will be monitored for concussion symptoms.
